scope: mcp-bpmn-3cw file-operation containment and TOCTOU hardening
intent: Prevent BPMN and Mermaid file tools from escaping the configured diagrams root, including synchronized root and leaf replacement races, while preserving valid operations and persistence semantics.
applied_fixes: Pinned each FileManager to one root device/inode identity and retained that identity across failed operations and retries.
Routed BPMN reads, Mermaid reads, writes, and deletes through one shared SafeFileStore.
Performed basename-only operations in a cwd-anchored helper with no-follow/post-open identity checks and atomic entry-relative writes/deletes.
Reused the helper during mutation bursts and added bounded idle shutdown after the initial per-operation process design regressed the resource-limit test timeout.
Added synchronized root/leaf swap, retry, cross-interface, atomic no-clobber, and staging-failure regressions.
residual_risks: The configured root identity is trusted at first successful resolution, so its parent must not be writable by an untrusted local principal beforehand.

A same-account process can still race which in-root entry occupies a basename; the containment guarantee prevents redirection to an outside path rather than serializing hostile same-account filesystem mutation.
testing_gaps: Windows traversal/drive/UNC forms are table-tested, but synchronized runtime replacement tests were executed on macOS rather than a Windows host.
validation: focused file security, FileManager, persistence, and resource-exhaustion suites
